rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bare رويد occupies the position of a verb and means أرود in commands such as رويد زيدا.
rows.anchor: تقول رويد زيدا وإنما تريد أرود زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رويد can modify an explicit verbal noun as an adverb, or stand alone with the verbal noun omitted; with an expressed noun it can function in more than one way.
rows.anchor: ويكون رويد أيضا صفة كقولك ساروا سيرا رويدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached kaf in رويدك specifies or emphasizes the addressee, distinguishing a particular listener when the form itself does not mark person or number.
rows.anchor: أدخل الكاف حين خاف التباس من يعنى بمن لا يعنى وإنما حذفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kaf is neither a subject marker nor a noun: the implicit command subject is a doer, and treating kaf as a noun creates impossible constructions.
rows.anchor: المضمرين ها هنا فاعلون وعلامة المضمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs also use رويد نفسه as a verbal noun, like the Qur'anic مصدر فضرب الرقاب and the poetic عذير الحي.
rows.anchor: من يقول رويد نفسه جعله مصدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In هلم لك, unlike رويدك, kaf is a genitive noun after لام; its meaning still adds specification or emphasis.
rows.anchor: هلم لك فالكاف ههنا اسم مجرور باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a hidden nominative addressee, coordination and emphasis are smoother when that pronoun is made explicit, as in رويدكم أنتم وعبد الله.
rows.anchor: وتقول فيما يكون معطوفا على الاسم المضمر فى النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A visible noun cannot coordinate directly with the genitive kaf in هلم لك; it can instead coordinate with the understood nominative addressee, made explicit by أنت.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تعطف على الكاف المجرورة الاسم لأنك لا تعطف المظهر على المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an accusative noun is followed by another coordinated noun, accusative is preferred if both are construed with the verb; Qur'anic examples include ثمودا, فريقا, and الظالمين.
rows.anchor: النصب ههنا لأن الاسم الأول مبنى على الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same verb based accusative coordination works with كان and ليس, which behave like verbs in their government.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك كنت أخاك وزيدا كنت له أخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the second noun is also good when it begins an independent clause; it is more natural the closer that noun stands to the beginning.
rows.anchor: كأنك قلت لقيت زيدا وعمرو أفضل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In يغشى طائفة منكم وطائفة قد أهمتهم أنفسهم, the second واو begins a new clause, not a coordinated object; the second phrase describes a circumstance.
rows.anchor: وإنما هى واو الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ولكن or بل, the second noun follows the same accusative or permitted nominative patterns as a noun joined by ordinary conjunctions, since these particles govern nothing.
rows.anchor: لأن بل ولكن لا تعملان شيئا وتشركان الآخر مع الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ظن, حسب, خال, أرى, رأى, or زعم is operative, it governs like other verbs; its object and predicate can both be accusative, including under fronting or questions.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاءت مستعملة فهى بمنزلة رأيت وضربت وأعطيت فى الإعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verbs can be canceled parenthetically, leaving the following predicate nominative; delaying the verb makes cancellation strongest because the statement begins in certainty before doubt is added.
rows.anchor: وكلما أردت الإلغاء فالتأخير أقوى

rows.speaker: اللعين
rows.claim: Al-Laʿīn's line about the rajaz poems uses خلت parenthetically, with اللؤم والخور nominative; it illustrates canceled government.
rows.anchor: وفى الأراجيز خلت اللؤم والخور

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's تزعميني and al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī's أزعمك are poetic evidence that زعم can remain operative and govern its complements.
rows.anchor: فإن تزعمينى كنت أجهل فيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In questions with أين or هل, the interrogative does not prevent the following material from being analyzed as an initial clause; forms such as أين ترى زيدا allow the relevant accusative or nominative patterns.
rows.anchor: لأن هل وأين كأنك لم تذكرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قال introduces a complete quoted utterance, so the quotation retains its independent syntax; the angels' statement to Mary consequently takes إن الله, not أن الله.
rows.anchor: وتصديق ذلك قوله جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative تقول is treated like تظن, not ظننت: speakers usually ask about their own belief, while the basic role of قال is to introduce an independent quotation.
rows.anchor: إلا تقول فى الاستفهام شبهوها بتظن

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: A dialect of Banū Sulaym, whose Arabic Sībawayh trusts, treats the باب قلت like ظننت and its government.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو الخطاب وسألته عنه غير مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun ظن can also be canceled; it is awkward sentence initially, but more acceptable after interrogative material or an existing clause.
rows.anchor: المصدر قد يلغى كما يلغى الفعل وذلك قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In عبد الله أظنه منطلق, the pronoun can refer to the implicit source ذاك الظن rather than Abdullah; explicit ذاك is clearer and preferable to ظني.
rows.anchor: هذه الهاء على ذاك كأنك قلت زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When أن supplies a sufficient complement, ظننت أنه منطلق can be shortened to أظن أنه فاعل and needs no second predicate.
rows.anchor: فأما ظننت أنه منطلق فاستغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a reply to من تظن, ظننت زيدا means I suspect or accuse Zayd; ظنين likewise means accused.
rows.anchor: فتقول ظننت زيدا كأنه قال أتهمت زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says ذاك is not used in the same way with حسب, خال, and أرى, since Arabic may admit a construction with one verb but not its semantic peers.
rows.anchor: ولم يجعلوا ذاك فى حسبت وخلت وأرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative pronouns such as أيهم, من, and ما are themselves clause beginnings; the verb normally follows them directly, with an object after it accusative, while poetry may front that object by necessity.
rows.anchor: هو حرف الاستفهام لا تدخل عليه الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When adjacent wāw and yāʾ meet in the described environments, they tend to become yāʾ because they share an articulation and yāʾ is lighter, resembling alif.
rows.anchor: الياء الغالبة في القلب لا الواو لأنها أخف عليهم لشبهها بالألف

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes سيد as فيعل, allowing a morphological pattern restricted to weak roots; Sībawayh prefers this account, supported by other weak-only forms and unbroken فتح in هيبان وتيحان.
rows.anchor: وكان الخليل يقول سيد فيعل وإن

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another analysis also calls سيد فيعل but explains its altered vowel by analogy with forms whose vowel changes when a noun changes; Sībawayh favors al-Khalīl's weak-root pattern analysis.
rows.anchor: وقد قال غيره هو فيعل لأنه ليس في غير المعتل فيعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ميت, هين, and لين, the medial weak consonant is deleted; the same deletion occurs in longer weak forms such as كينونة and قيدودة to avoid a crowd of yāʾ sounds.
rows.anchor: وهين ولين فإنهم يحذفون العين كما يحذفون الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as ديار and قيام reflect waw-to-yāʾ change from underlying ديوار and قيوام; قيوم and ديور similarly reflect underlying doubled-vowel forms on فيعال and فيعول.
rows.anchor: ومما قلبوا الواو فيه ياء ديار وقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waw is not changed in صيود and طويل when the first of the adjacent letters is moving: assimilation requires the first letter to be still, so the original form remains.
rows.anchor: صيود وطويل وأشباه ذلك فإنما منعهم أن يقلبوا الواو فيهن ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nonroot waw inserted by the pattern in سوير and بويع is not assimilated, since it can disappear in related forms; قوول and تقوول preserve length rather than merging the waws.
rows.anchor: فقال لأن هذه الواو ليست بلازمة ولا بأصل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some speakers say ريا and رية, treating the waw left after dropping hamza as original; Sībawayh distinguishes this from سوير, whose waw substitutes for alif.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم ريا ورية فجعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ of ديوان is not integral: its plural and diminutive recover waw, so it does not trigger assimilation; a true فيعال formation would assimilate.
rows.anchor: يقولون دويوين في التحقير ودواوين في الجمع
